newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK inflation drops to 2.7 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK inflation drops to 2.7 percent in February.

text.p: Britain's inflation rate fell to 2.7 percent in the year to February from 2.8 in January, official data showed on Thursday, providing a welcome boost for the government in the first days of its election campaign.

The Office for National Statistics said the government's preferred measured of underlying inflation, which excludes home loan payments, dropped to 2.9 percent year-on-year in February from 3.1, bringing it closer to the official 2.5 percent target.
"We are steadily getting to our inflation target which we will maintain throughout the next Parliament," Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke said.
"This is a central foundation which we have put in place for a recovery which will last."
On Monday, Prime Minister John Major called an election for May 1.
Economists had expected underlying inflation, known as RPIX, to tumble to 2.9 percent but thought the headline figure would hold steady at 2.8.

"If anything the numbers are slightly better than the market was looking for," said Peter Osler, economist at GNI. "They will take some of the heat off the Chancellor after the very strong figures we saw yesterday."
Strong earnings growth and a sharp fall in unemployment revealed in figures on Wednesday led to concern the economy was overheating and an interest rate rise might be needed soon.
Minutes from the early February monetary meeting between Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George showed the Bank wishes to see base rates put up to 6.25 percent, from six, immediately.
The Office for National Statistics said the fall in RPIX was largely due to lower food prices. But it warned seasonal food prices tend to rise in March.

A 1.5 percent leap in clothing and footwear prices and a 0.8 percent climb in the prices of household goods suggest demand on the high street remains buoyant. But consumers are still only parting with money if the price is right.
"The overall picture is still one of consumer resistance to price hikes which will be key to keeping inflation down," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser to BankAmerica.
